name: Lathe

hero.title: 121 lines of OpenAPI in. 1,133 lines of typed client you never write.
hero.lede: Lathe turns your OpenAPI spec into validated schemas, typed endpoints and query hooks for Pyreon, plus mocks, fake-data factories, docs and MCP tools. It fails CI when the committed client is stale, names every hook a breaking spec change touches, and can emit native modules that it compiles for iOS and Android before telling you they work.

why.title: Your API client, generated and kept honest.

items.title: One spec, the whole surface
items.text: Schemas, a typed client, `useQuery` and `useMutation` hooks with their query keys, deterministic mocks, `createBook(overrides?)` factories, Atlas scenarios, Markdown docs and MCP tool definitions. Fixtures live in `./gen/dev`, which `./gen/index.ts` never imports, so they cannot reach a page bundle.

items.title: API changes show up in the PR
items.text: `lathe diff main:openapi.yaml openapi.yaml --format github` puts breaking changes first, each naming the generated code it affects: "affects createBook, useCreateBook (books); getBook, useGetBook (books); listBooks, useListBooks (books)".

items.title: Responses are checked, not trusted
items.text: Every response is validated against the generated schema by default (`responseValidation: 'strict'`), so a backend that drifts fails at the boundary instead of three components later. `'warn'` and `'off'` exist when you need them.

items.title: Switch without a rewrite weekend
items.text: `lathe init` reads your orval, hey-api or kubb config, or the openapi-typescript script in package.json, maps it, and lists what it could not map with what to do instead. It never runs your old config and never writes into the old generator's output.

difference.title: The client you hand-write today, and the one line that replaces it.

before.label: React + TanStack Query, by hand
before.caption: A type copied from the docs, a key to keep in sync, a body nobody checks.

after.label: Pyreon + Lathe
after.caption: URL, method, key and schema come from the spec. The response is validated.

comingFrom.title: Same hooks, read as signals. No `.data.data`.
comingFrom.note: Hook arguments are an accessor, so a new `bookId` refetches. Mutation bodies say their encoding: `json`, `form`, `multipart` or `body`. `lathe init` maps `client: 'react-query'` to `plugins: queries`, `mock: true` to `mocks, faker`, and lists `override.mutator` for you to move into `configureApi({ use })`.

comingFrom.title: Call the operation by name, not by path string.
comingFrom.note: Path parameters are `params`, query parameters `query`, the body `json`. There is no `{ data, error }` pair: the call resolves to the validated body and rejects on a non-2xx status with the status and parsed body. `lathe init` finds the `openapi-typescript spec -o file` script and reads the paths from it.

comingFrom.title: A generated hook instead of an options factory to spread.
comingFrom.note: `@hey-api/sdk` maps to `plugins: client`, `@tanstack/react-query` to `queries`, `zod` to `validator: 'zod'`. A mutation already invalidates the reads it can change (`createBook` refetches `getBook` and `listBooks`); pass `invalidates` to change that.

real output

Delete one enum value from the spec. Here is what CI sees.

The repo's examples/lathe-bookshelf, with lost removed from Book.status and the client not regenerated. Every line below is what the command printed.

$ lathe check
lathe / Bookshelf 1.2.0
  4 models  4 operations  target=multiplatform
  plugins: schemas, client, queries, mocks, faker, atlas, docs (+components - required by them)

  (25 unchanged files, one "·" line each, omitted)
  ~ src/gen/schemas/Book.ts
  ~ src/gen/faker.ts
  ~ src/gen/docs/models.md
  ~ src/gen/api-surface.json

  0 of 29 file(s) written

  contract  1 breaking  0 additive
    ! [field-type-changed] Book.status enum("available"|"borrowed"|"lost") → enum("available"|"borrowed")

  native reach  3/4 operations
    web-only 1 op(s): createBook
      `POST` lowers through mutations, which PMTC does not yet recognise; GET operations on this client DO reach native.

  lowers authors.native.tsx swift  [PyreonQuery< PyreonZodSchema_ PyreonSchemaError]  compiled
  lowers authors.native.tsx kotlin  [PyreonQuery< PyreonZodSchema_ PyreonSchemaError]  compiled
  lowers books.native.tsx swift  [PyreonQuery< PyreonZodSchema_ PyreonSchemaError]  compiled
  lowers books.native.tsx kotlin  [PyreonQuery< PyreonZodSchema_ PyreonSchemaError]  compiled
  all modules together swift  compiled
  all modules together kotlin  compiled

  STALE: 4 generated file(s) differ from the spec:
    schemas/Book.ts
    faker.ts
    docs/models.md
    api-surface.json

  Fix: run `lathe generate` and commit the result.
$ echo $?
1

demo.title: Pick what to generate.
demo.text: Choose plugins. Lathe adds whatever they import and tells you what came along. The file list is what `lathe generate` writes for the Bookshelf example spec.

demo.spec: Dependencies are the real plugin graph (packages/tools/lathe/src/core/config.ts): client→schemas, queries→client, mocks→client, faker→schemas, components→queries, atlas→components+mocks, mcp→client; types and docs stand alone. File names and counts are exactly what `lathe generate --target web --plugins <selection>` writes for examples/lathe-bookshelf/openapi.yaml: `queries` alone is 17 files, all ten plugins are 29. `dev.ts` appears when mocks or faker is selected; index.ts, package.json, lathe-manifest.json and api-surface.json always. The header line uses the CLI's own format: "plugins: atlas (+schemas, +client, +queries, +components, +mocks - required by them)". The demo should call `generate()` from `@pyreon/lathe/core` on the bundled spec rather than hard-code the map, if bundle size allows.

items.name: `lathe init`
items.text: detects orval, hey-api, kubb or openapi-typescript and writes the `lathe` section of `pyreon.config.ts`

items.name: `lathe check`
items.text: regenerates in memory and exits 1 when the committed client is stale

items.name: `lathe diff`
items.text: breaking and additive contract changes as text, Markdown, GitHub annotations or JSON

items.name: Vite plugin
items.text: `@pyreon/lathe/vite` regenerates on spec changes; `checkOnBuild` turns a stale client into a build error

items.name: Four HTTP clients
items.text: `pyreon`, `fetch`, `axios` or `ky`; every file except `client.ts`, `mocks.ts` and `dev.ts` is byte-identical across them

items.name: Streams
items.text: Server-Sent Events and NDJSON as validated async iterators and `use<Op>Stream` signals, with reconnect and `Last-Event-ID`

items.name: Webhooks
items.text: typed payloads and a `webhookHandler` that calls your own signature check and caps bodies at 1 MiB

items.name: MCP tools
items.text: each JSON-callable operation as a tool definition whose `call` runs the generated endpoint through your auth and middleware

items.name: Loss notes
items.text: anything the spec says that the client cannot honour becomes a note with a stable code and a JSON pointer

api.title: Flags, plugins, config and what the client exports.

limits.title: Response headers are not generated
limits.text: They are reported as a `response-headers` loss note. Header and cookie parameters are typed call arguments.

limits.title: Mutations stay on the web
limits.text: The native compiler lowers reads, not mutations, so each `POST` is reported `web-only` with that reason. GET operations and typed streams reach native, and only with an absolute `baseUrl`.

limits.title: No surprise network calls
limits.text: A remote `$ref` is reported, not fetched, until you set `remoteRefs: 'fetch'` or run `lathe pull`.

limits.title: Webhook signatures are your hook
limits.text: `webhookHandler` calls your `verify`; it does not know any vendor's signing scheme.

related.name: Query
related.text: The generated hooks are `@pyreon/query` hooks, keys included.

related.name: Atlas
related.text: Browse every generated read with mocked data in the workbench.

recipes.title: An API contract check on every pull request
recipes.text: `lathe diff` takes git refs. Breaking changes become `::error` annotations on the PR, and `lathe check` fails if someone edited the spec without regenerating.
recipes.code:
# .github/workflows/api-contract.yml
name: API contract
on:
  pull_request:
    paths: ['openapi.yaml']
jobs:
  contract:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
      - run: bun install
      - run: bunx lathe diff origin/main:openapi.yaml openapi.yaml --format github --fail-on-breaking
      - run: bunx lathe check

recipes.title: Tests against the spec, no server, no MSW
recipes.text: Mocks are middleware on the generated client, so they behave the same in node and the browser. Factories respect the spec's constraints and are reproducible from a seed. This file passes under vitest against the Bookshelf client.

recipes.title: Auth that follows the signed-in user
recipes.text: `headers` is re-read on every request, so a new token applies to the next call. Middleware wraps every request, streams included.

faq.q: Do I have to keep orval (or hey-api) installed during the move?
faq.a: No. `lathe init` reads the old config as text and never runs it. If the old output directory still holds the old client, Lathe writes beside it so the app keeps working until your imports move.

faq.q: Will mocks and fake data end up in my production bundle?
faq.a: They cannot. `./gen/index.ts` never names `./mocks`, `./faker` or `./components`, so no import edge exists for a bundler to follow, and the generated `package.json` declares `sideEffects` so the rest tree-shakes. The Bookshelf example checks it: `grep -c '@faker-js' dist/assets/*.js` prints 0.

faq.q: What happens to the parts of my spec Lathe cannot represent?
faq.a: Each one becomes a note with a stable code (`response-headers`, `unsupported-security`, `int64-precision`…), a JSON pointer into the spec and a severity. They print in the terminal and land in the generated reference pages under "Not represented".

faq.q: Which operations reach iOS and Android?
faq.a: With `target: 'multiplatform'` and an absolute `baseUrl`: GET operations (path parameters become component props) and typed SSE or NDJSON streams. Mutations stay web-only. Lathe runs the native compiler over its own output, checks for the lowering markers, and type-checks with `swiftc` and `kotlinc` when they are installed; without the compiler it says the check was skipped. The native targets are experimental.

faq.q: Can I add my own output?
faq.a: Yes. A `--plugins` entry that is not a built-in name is loaded as a plugin module (a path or a package), written with `definePlugin` from `@pyreon/lathe/core`.

end.title: Your spec already knows the API. Let it write the client.
